- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >0.8) and forecast spikes upward, reduce the peak by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- If sentiment turns negative (e.g., <0.2) and forecast is high, apply downward bias of 3–7% to reflect risk aversion.  
- Model tends to overestimate early in the 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or slightly positive — adjust downward by 2–5% for days 1–7.  
- Overshoots after sharp sentiment-driven spikes (e.g., +0.6 to +0.8) often persist for 2–3 days — dampen forecast by 1–3% per day until sentiment stabilizes.  
- Mean reversion is stronger in the final 7–10 days of the 30-day horizon — if forecast is above 10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 1–3% per day.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated short-term volatility (e.g., alternating +0.5 and -0.3), model should smooth transitions — avoid abrupt 5–10% swings in consecutive days.
